title: I built an MT5 Gold EA with prop-firm drawdown protection — looking for honest feedback
author: Due_Cauliflower1453
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’m the developer of **Sycz HolyGrail**, an automated EA built specifically for **XAUUSD on MetaTrader 5**.

I want to be transparent from the beginning: **this is my own commercial EA**, currently listed on the MQL5 Market. I’m posting here because I’d like feedback from people who actually use EAs and automated systems rather than just posting another advertisement.

One of the main things I focused on during development was **risk management for prop-firm accounts**.

The EA includes:

* 9 internal Gold trading modules
* Adaptive position sizing
* Daily equity drawdown protection
* Overall account drawdown protection
* End-of-day trailing drawdown protection
* Configurable challenge profit target
* Automatic trading lock when protection limits are reached
* Pending-order removal and position management when a protection condition triggers
* News, spread, weekend and free-margin protections

For example, if a prop firm has a **5% daily-loss limit**, the EA can be configured to react earlier, such as around **4%**, instead of deliberately using the entire available drawdown.

The idea is to leave some margin for things like spread, commission, slippage and rapid XAUUSD movements.

I’m **not claiming that this guarantees passing a prop-firm challenge**. Prop-firm rules vary, execution conditions vary, and automated risk controls cannot eliminate trading risk.

The EA is also new, so I’m not going to pretend I have years of live results. At the moment I’m continuing backtesting, forward testing and gathering user feedback.

If anyone here runs automated Gold strategies or EAs on prop firms, I’d genuinely be interested in hearing what you think about the protection approach — especially daily drawdown versus trailing drawdown management.

For anyone who wants to look at the actual EA and settings:

**Sycz HolyGrail – MQL5 Market**  
[https://www.mql5.com/en/market/product/197337](https://www.mql5.com/en/market/product/197337?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Current price: **$99**

Happy to answer technical questions about the risk-management system or how the EA reacts when its protection limits are approached.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: one check on the daily protection: most prop firms measure the daily and trailing limits on equity including open floating, and a few reset from balance at 5pm server time rather than midnight. an EA that locks on closed losses at 4% can still get breached by an open gold position moving 1% against you in a minute, so the lock needs to read floating equity and the firm's reset time, not the calendar day.

replies.author: Due_Cauliflower1453
replies.body: true we did that our prop firm calculation based on equity not on the balance and we kept in mind floating equity

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: good, floating equity is the one that catches most people. the 5pm server reset is the other, worth a look if you haven't already.

replies.author: Due_Cauliflower1453
replies.body: thanks for the headsup i did focus on propfirm TOS and how they work to figure how  should my EA react to them so far my ea pass FTMO trial with 0.7% DD also for my Propfirm settings my EA calculate LOT size from max DD  not from the balance if my settings is 2.5DD and my account is 100k lots size calculated from 2.5k so even the EA lose all the trades i only lose 2.5k USD for that day

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: sizing off the max daily loss instead of the balance is the right way round, most EAs I see do it backwards. 0.7% on the trial is a clean run.

replies.author: Due_Cauliflower1453
replies.body: yeah also my logic was keeping my trading logic clean while my propfirm settings playing with the lots to keep it less then max DD

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Keeping the logic clean and letting the prop settings own the lots also means you backtest the logic once and then lay every firm's drawdown rules on top without rerunning the whole thing. That split pays off the day you switch firms.
